finding.problem: The six-blocker blueprint correctly requires exact queued+buffered+graph/device timing, but these pw_time terms are not natively one interchangeable frame unit. Raw addition of queued, buffered and delay would be wrong whenever application/source rate, stream samplerate and graph rate differ.
finding.terminal_risk: A superficially exact timed-stream helper could still mint a false bound or wrong cancel_source_frame under resampling if it sums frame/tick counts without first converting each term through its documented time domain.

official_pipewire_formula.queued_ms: pw_time.queued * 1000 / app_rate, only when the helper deliberately sets pw_buffer.size in audio frames; PipeWire documents pw_time.queued as the sum of application-chosen pw_buffer.size units.
official_pipewire_formula.buffered_ms: pw_time.buffered * 1000 / stream_samplerate for audio/raw; buffered is resampler/converter frames.
official_pipewire_formula.graph_delay_ms: max(0, pw_time.delay - elapsed) * 1000 * pw_time.rate.num / pw_time.rate.denom; negative effective graph delay may be clamped to zero per PipeWire timing semantics.

required_helper_contract_precision: Set pw_buffer.size to the exact number of application/source audio frames queued in each buffer. Persist this unit choice explicitly in every timing receipt.
Persist app_rate/source_rate, negotiated stream_samplerate and pw_time.rate.num/denom independently; never assume they are equal merely because the input WAV is fixed-rate.
Persist pw_time.now, ticks, delay, queued, buffered, queued_buffers, size, pw_stream_get_nsec and the helper monotonic snapshot timestamp from the same exact running stream epoch.

Normalize queued, buffered and graph delay to time (prefer integer/rational nanoseconds or microseconds internally) before combining them. Convert to source frames only after the time-domain sum is fixed.
Do not use pw_time.ticks alone as source-frame position. Graph ticks are the graph driver's timeline, not automatically the application/source sample index.

If the helper uses source_frames_submitted to derive a presentation-relative source position, the only admissible derived form is based on exact source-frame accounting minus normalized not-yet-presented duration converted back at source_rate; mark this mapping DERIVED and independently validate it against monitor PCM alignment.

If any app-rate/stream-rate/graph-rate relationship or buffering unit is ambiguous, classify EVIDENCE_INVALID_TIMING_UNIT_AMBIGUITY and stop before promotion-bearing cancel/PRODUCT_NEGATIVE reasoning.

derived_source_position_rule.precondition: source_frames_submitted is exact and monotonic; pw_buffer.size is source/application frames; all timing terms belong to the same exact stream snapshot/epoch.
derived_source_position_rule.important_fence: This candidate must not become terminal authority until Trigger4 proves startup-delay invariance, rate-conversion correctness and agreement with independent monitor PCM alignment. If it cannot be uniquely validated, fail closed rather than guessing.

focused_regressions: Same queued/buffered/delay wall-clock durations represented at different app/stream/graph rates must yield the same total_playback_delay_ms within declared integer rounding policy.
Raw numerical equality of frame counts at 22050 Hz and 48000 Hz must NOT be treated as equal duration.
Changing only graph rate representation while preserving physical duration must not change the frozen bound.
Changing only helper process startup delay while preserving exact stream/source progression must not move derived cancel_source_frame.
Ambiguous pw_buffer.size units or missing stream_samplerate must fail closed as EVIDENCE_INVALID_TIMING_UNIT_AMBIGUITY.
Derived source position must agree with independent monitor PCM source alignment inside a predeclared tolerance; disagreement is evidence-invalid, not product-negative.
next_action: Trigger4 folds this unit-normalization rule into the existing six-blocker timed-stream repair and R1-R12-or-stricter regression set before one fresh exact S2 dispatch.
